paragraphs.title: David Is Anointed King over Judah

easy.explanation: David enquired of the LORD before going to Judah.
easy.q: Whom did David ask whether he should go up to Judah?

easy.explanation: The LORD told David to go to Hebron.
easy.q: To which city did the LORD tell David to go?

easy.explanation: The men of Judah anointed David king.
easy.q: Who anointed David king over the house of Judah?

answers: His two wives and his men
medium.explanation: David went up with his two wives, his men, and their households.
medium.q: Who went up to Hebron with David?

answers: Because they had made him king
medium.explanation: David praised them for showing kindness to Saul and burying him.
medium.q: Why did David bless the men of Jabesh-gilead?

medium.explanation: David encouraged the men to strengthen their hands and be courageous.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “be ye valiant” mean?

answers: He wanted to act according to God's direction
He did not know the way to Hebron
He was waiting for Abner's approval
challenge.explanation: David sought God's guidance before taking action.
challenge.q: What does David's enquiry of the LORD before going to Judah show?

answers: David was angry that they buried Saul
David viewed the burial as kindness and promised kindness in return
David asked them to move to Hebron
challenge.explanation: David blessed them for their kindness and promised to requite it.
challenge.q: What connection is made between Saul's burial and David's response to Jabesh-gilead?

answers: He went from being pursued to being king over Judah
He went from captain to king over all Israel
He went from a Judean to king of Jabesh-gilead
challenge.explanation: The men of Judah anointed David king over the house of Judah.
challenge.q: How did David's status change in these verses?

easy.explanation: Abner took Ish-bosheth and brought him to Mahanaim.
easy.q: Who brought Ish-bosheth over to Mahanaim?

easy.explanation: Ish-bosheth was made king over Israel and its listed regions and tribes.
easy.q: Over whom was Ish-bosheth made king?

easy.explanation: David reigned in Hebron for seven years and six months.
easy.q: How long did David reign in Hebron over Judah?

answers: David ruled Israel and Ish-bosheth ruled Judah
David ruled Judah and Ish-bosheth ruled Israel
medium.explanation: The house of Judah followed David, while Ish-bosheth was made king over Israel.
medium.q: What was the difference between David's kingdom and Ish-bosheth's kingdom?

answers: Abner had a central role in establishing Ish-bosheth's rule
Abner was one of David's wives
medium.explanation: The passage specifically says that Abner took Ish-bosheth and made him king.
medium.q: What can be inferred from Abner making Ish-bosheth king?

answers: The men of Judah supported David's rule
The men of Judah pursued David
The men of Judah left Hebron
medium.explanation: Judah remained loyal to and followed David.
medium.q: What does “the house of Judah followed David” mean?

answers: One king ruled all Israel without opposition
Two competing kingdoms existed: David in Judah and Ish-bosheth in Israel
Abner and Joab shared the rule
challenge.explanation: David ruled Judah while Ish-bosheth was made king over Israel.
challenge.q: What political situation is described in these verses?

answers: They ruled for the same length of time
challenge.explanation: Ish-bosheth reigned two years, while David reigned in Hebron seven years and six months.
challenge.q: What does the difference in their reigns show?

answers: The passage lists Gilead, the Ashurites, Jezreel, Ephraim, Benjamin, and Israel
challenge.explanation: The passage names several regions and tribes over which Ish-bosheth was made king.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that Ish-bosheth's kingdom included many regions and tribes?

paragraphs.title: The Confrontation at the Pool of Gibeon

answers: Abner and the servants of Ish-bosheth
easy.explanation: Abner and Ish-bosheth's servants went from Mahanaim to Gibeon.
easy.q: Who went out from Mahanaim to Gibeon?

easy.explanation: They met beside the pool of Gibeon.
easy.q: Where did Joab's men and Abner's men meet?

easy.explanation: Abner made this proposal to Joab.
easy.q: Who suggested that the young men arise and play before them?

answers: Three hundred and threescore from each side
medium.explanation: Twelve of Benjamin and twelve of David's servants went over.
medium.q: How many young men came from each side in the first contest?

answers: Each caught his fellow by the head and they fell together
medium.explanation: Each man thrust his sword into his fellow, and they fell down together.
medium.q: How did the contest of the young men end?

answers: David's men were defeated by Israel
The battle ended without a victor
Abner and the men of Israel were beaten before David's servants
medium.explanation: The passage says that Abner and the men of Israel were beaten.
medium.q: What was the result of the battle that followed?

answers: A seemingly limited encounter became deadly and turned into real warfare
challenge.explanation: The contest was followed by a very sore battle.
challenge.q: What does the change from a contest to a battle reveal?

challenge.explanation: The place was called Helkath-hazzurim, which was in Gibeon.
challenge.q: What name was given to the place where the young men fell?

answers: They faced one another before the confrontation
They had already withdrawn from battle
They were in separate camps with no contact
challenge.explanation: The passage describes the two groups sitting opposite one another by the pool.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the two armies sitting on opposite sides of the pool?

easy.explanation: The three sons were Joab, Abishai, and Asahel.
easy.q: Who were the three sons of Zeruiah mentioned here?

answers: The hinder end of a spear
easy.explanation: Abner struck Asahel under the fifth rib with the hinder end of his spear.
easy.q: With what did Abner strike Asahel?

answers: Abner stopped and waited for him
medium.explanation: Asahel was as light of foot as a wild roe.
medium.q: Why was Asahel able to pursue Abner so quickly?

answers: Turn aside and take the armour of another young man
medium.explanation: Abner told him to turn right or left and take another young man's armour.
medium.q: What did Abner tell Asahel to do?

medium.explanation: Abner urged Asahel to stop following him and turn aside.
medium.q: What does “turn aside” mean in this passage?

answers: He wanted to avoid the encounter and keep from harming him
He wanted Asahel to join him
He did not know who was following him
challenge.explanation: Abner repeatedly urged Asahel to turn aside and asked how he could face Joab afterward.
challenge.q: Why did Abner warn Asahel before striking him?

answers: He refused to stop pursuing Abner
He was injured while burying Saul
challenge.explanation: Asahel would not turn aside, so Abner struck him with the spear.
challenge.q: What ultimately led to Asahel's death?

challenge.explanation: Everyone who came to the place where Asahel fell stood still.
challenge.q: What did those who came to the place of Asahel's death do?

paragraphs.title: The Pursuit Ends and Abner Withdraws

answers: David and the men of Jabesh-gilead
Ish-bosheth and the men of Judah
easy.q: Who pursued Abner after Asahel's death?

easy.explanation: The children of Benjamin gathered after Abner.
easy.q: Who gathered themselves together around Abner?

easy.explanation: Joab blew a trumpet, and the people stopped pursuing.
easy.q: How did Joab announce the end of the pursuit?

answers: He knew that continuing the conflict would end in bitterness
He wanted to reach Hebron before night
The children of Benjamin had deserted him
medium.explanation: Abner warned that the outcome would be bitterness in the latter end.
medium.q: Why did Abner call for the pursuit to stop?

answers: The people stood still and fought no more
medium.explanation: The people pursued Israel no more and fought no more.
medium.q: What happened after Joab blew the trumpet?

medium.explanation: Abner asked whether the fighting would continue without end.
medium.q: What does “Shall the sword devour for ever?” mean?

answers: Joab ignored Abner and continued the pursuit
Joab accepted Abner's words and stopped the pursuit
challenge.explanation: After Abner spoke, Joab blew the trumpet and ended the pursuit.
challenge.q: What connection is there between Abner's warning and Joab's action?

answers: Through the plain, over Jordan, and to Mahanaim
challenge.explanation: They walked through the plain, passed over Jordan, went through Bithron, and came to Mahanaim.
challenge.q: In which direction did Abner and his men withdraw?

answers: They organized themselves to support Abner
challenge.explanation: The Benjaminites gathered together after Abner and stood as one troop.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the children of Benjamin becoming one troop on a hill?

paragraphs.title: The Battle's Results and Asahel's Burial

easy.explanation: Nineteen of David's servants were missing, in addition to Asahel.
easy.q: How many of David's servants were missing besides Asahel?

easy.explanation: Three hundred and threescore men of Abner died.
easy.q: How many of Abner's men died?

answers: In his father's sepulchre at Bethlehem
easy.explanation: Asahel was buried in his father's sepulchre in Bethlehem.

answers: Both sides had the same losses
medium.explanation: David lost nineteen men and Asahel, while Abner lost three hundred and threescore men.
medium.q: What was the difference in casualties between the two sides?

answers: At break of day, after traveling all night
medium.explanation: They went all night and came to Hebron at break of day.
medium.q: When did Joab and his men arrive at Hebron?

medium.explanation: Joab gathered the people and determined how many were missing.
medium.q: What does “there lacked” mean in this context?

answers: Joab returned, counted his men, Asahel was buried, and the warriors reached Hebron
Asahel was buried, and then the battle began
Abner's men reached Hebron and buried Asahel
challenge.explanation: The passage records the return, the count of losses, Asahel's burial, and the arrival at Hebron.
challenge.q: Which sequence of events is described at the end of the chapter?

answers: They cared for him and brought him to a family burial place
They left him where he fell
challenge.explanation: Asahel was taken and buried in his father's sepulchre at Bethlehem.
challenge.q: What does Asahel's burial in his father's sepulchre show about his family?

answers: It shows the cost of war through deaths, burial, and the weary return to Hebron
It shows that there were no casualties
It cancels the account of the battle
challenge.explanation: The final verses summarize the casualties, Asahel's burial, and the armies' return.
challenge.q: How does the chapter's ending connect with the earlier battle?
